title: The Marangoni rods' swim-before-divide minority is not inherited: it is redrawn every cycle, speed (not distance) is selected, and divisions stop at saturation after about 2 generations
summary: Over 102 dividing tracks on 7 runs of c34's Marangoni world (seeds 51, 52, a 1.5x grid, and fresh seeds 61-64), the distance a rod swims between its own birth and division, in its own lengths (median 1.42), shows no parent-offspring relation (slope +0.22 [-0.61, +1.44], n=25 pairs; null +0.08) and sisters are no more alike than unrelated rods. The 5 rods that swim 3 or more lengths (seeds 61, 62 twice, 63, 64) are rods born small that get a long cycle without slowing down; 4 of 5 are trailing daughters. Faster rods grow faster, divide sooner (rho -0.58) and leave more descendants (rho +0.26), so speed is selected but distance per cycle stays capped. The bath pins the total body matter, so bodies plateau at about 30 by frame 100 and only 4 of 145 later-born rods divide: a run spans about 2 generations. The minority persists because each cycle recreates it, not through lineages (report.md, files/results.txt).

finding.operator: Marangoni self-propulsion of active-nematic rods (the swim-before-divide minority)
finding.control: parent-offspring, sister and grandparent regressions against time-matched and time-and-place-matched unrelated pairs, bootstrap CIs
finding.result: D on D slope +0.22 [-0.61, +1.44] (n=25); speed slope +0.29 explained by timing (time null +0.33); sisters ICC over life -0.04; 5 of 102 dividing tracks reach D >= 3, all with long cycles; D falls from 1.63 to 1.01 between run halves; 4 of 145 rods born after frame 100 divide
